mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the simultaneous state where Team B's recent-5 corners FOR (8.4) is substantially above its all-prior average (5.731) AND Team A's recent-5 corners AGAINST (5.2) is above its all-prior average (4.721). Measure total corner volume in matches where both conditions hold jointly, versus matches where only one or neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner volume rises when both the attacking team's recent corner surge and the defending team's recent corner-concession surge are present simultaneously, compared to when only one condition is present.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production shows a sharp upward shift in recent form relative to its long-run average, while Team A's corner-kick concession shows a corresponding upward shift in recent form. The joint condition — attacker's recent corner surge AND defender's recent corner-concession surge — may amplify total corner volume beyond what either single-observable baseline predicts alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint evaluation of two distinct observable streams (Team B corners FOR recent vs. long-run AND Team A corners AGAINST recent vs. long-run) interacting multiplicatively. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band — it is a two-dimensional recent-form interaction across two different team roles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner production and concession by half. Condition on matches where Team B's first-half corner rate (FOR, H1) is above competition baseline AND Team A's second-half corner concession rate (AGAINST, H2) is above its own first-half concession rate. Measure whether the second half sees a disproportionate corner share relative to the first half in such configurations.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume is disproportionately elevated relative to first-half corner volume when the attacking team's first-half corner production is high and the defending team's second-half corner concession rate exceeds its first-half rate.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner production is asymmetrically split between halves: its first-half average (2.671) exceeds its second-half average (2.800 is close, but against Team A the second-half concession rate 2.367 is lower than first-half 2.291 — the asymmetry is cross-observable). Specifically, Team A concedes more corners in the second half than the first half, while Team B generates more corners in the first half. The joint half-level profile of attacker's first-half corner production versus defender's second-half corner concession creates a within-match distributional asymmetry that is not captured by full-match averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split conditioned on two distinct half-level observables from two different teams — it requires half resolution and a cross-team, cross-half joint condition, which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team's shots FOR is elevated above its long-run average while its shots_on_target FOR does not rise proportionally (i.e., shots-to-on-target ratio declines), AND the defending team's shots_on_target AGAINST is below its long-run average. Measure whether goals FOR the attacking team are suppressed in this joint configuration relative to what shot volume alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals for the attacking team are suppressed when shot volume is high but the shots-to-on-target ratio is declining and the opponent's shot-on-target concession rate is simultaneously improving — indicating a non-linear decoupling between shot volume and goal output.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots volume has surged sharply in recent form (recent-5: 17.6 vs. all-prior: 13.105) while its shots-on-target rate has not kept pace (recent-5: 4.8 vs. all-prior: 4.698). Simultaneously, Team B's shots-on-target concession has improved in recent form (recent-5: 3.8 vs. all-prior: 4.821). The joint condition of high shot volume with low conversion-to-on-target ratio for the attacker, combined with improved shot-on-target suppression by the defender, may indicate a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and shot quality that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for the attacker, combined with a third observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for the defender — a three-variable cross-team interaction that cannot be reduced to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B is playing away AND Team B's away foul rate is above the competition foul baseline. Within that condition, measure whether the combined foul volume (both teams) correlates with second-half card volume above the competition second-half card baseline. This is a two-dimensional conditioning: venue-specific foul asymmetry for Team B crossed with the joint foul environment.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises with the joint foul environment when Team B is playing away and its away foul rate is elevated above the competition baseline — with the relationship being stronger than what Team B's card rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls away from home (12.0) than at home (9.949), while Team A's foul production is relatively stable across venues (home: 10.465, away: 10.907). When Team B plays away and its foul rate is elevated, the joint foul environment (Team B fouls FOR away + Team A fouls FOR home) may interact with the second-half card rate. Specifically, a high combined foul environment in a match where Team B is away may predict elevated second-half cards beyond what either team's card baseline alone suggests.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) across two teams, with a venue-specific asymmetry for one team (Team B away fouls vs. home fouls) that is not symmetric. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the cross-observable foul-to-card relationship conditioned on venue-specific foul asymmetry.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both teams' offsides FOR are simultaneously below their respective long-run averages (a joint offside suppression state). Within that joint condition, measure whether goals and shots are also suppressed relative to competition baseline — testing whether the joint offside decline is a leading indicator of a low-intensity attacking match state.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals and shots are suppressed when both teams' offsides FOR are simultaneously below their long-run averages, suggesting a joint tactical retreat that reduces attacking intensity beyond what either team's individual goal or shot baseline predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has dropped sharply in recent form (recent-5: 1.0 vs. all-prior: 1.904, and vs. home all-prior: 2.146), while Team B's offsides FOR has also declined recently (recent-5: 1.6 vs. all-prior: 2.377). A joint decline in offsides for both teams simultaneously may indicate a shared tactical shift toward deeper, more cautious attacking lines — which in turn may correlate with lower goal totals and lower shot volumes, independent of what either team's goal or shot baseline alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint condition across two distinct observables (offsides for both teams simultaneously) used to predict a third observable (goals/shots), requiring a two-team, two-observable joint conditioning that cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.
